bugs.error_message: "שגיאה בשליחת ההזמנה. אנא נסה שוב." — checkout submission fails even after the logo upload (bug-095) was fixed
bugs.root_cause: orders table has RLS policy "orders: anon insert" (migration 001) but no table-level GRANT INSERT ON orders TO anon. Postgres checks GRANT privileges before RLS, so every anon checkout submission was rejected with "permission denied for table orders", caught by submitOrder and surfaced as a generic error. Exact same class of bug already fixed once for gallery_items (migration 004) — RLS policy alone is not sufficient in this project; anon needs an explicit GRANT.

bugs.error_message: Checkout submission still fails with the generic error after applying migrations 006 and 007 (user confirmed: "הרצתי את מיגרציות 6 ו7 ולא עזר")
bugs.root_cause: trg_orders_order_number only fires WHEN (NEW.order_number = ''). When order_number is omitted from an insert it defaults to NULL, and in SQL `NULL = ''` evaluates to NULL (not true), so the WHEN condition never matches and the trigger body never runs. app/admin/actions/create-order.ts (manual admin orders) explicitly inserts order_number: "" so it always worked; app/actions/submit-order.ts (public checkout) never set order_number at all, so orders.order_number's NOT NULL constraint rejected every public submission — a second, independent bug stacked on top of bug-096, present since the checkout was first built.
bugs.fix: 1) supabase/migrations/008_fix_order_number_trigger.sql: changed the trigger WHEN clause to `WHEN (NEW.order_number IS NULL OR NEW.order_number = '')`. 2) app/actions/submit-order.ts: explicitly insert order_number: "" to match the already-working admin pattern (belt-and-suspenders — either fix alone would have been enough).

bugs.root_cause: Postgres RLS filters the RETURNING clause of INSERT/UPDATE through the table's SELECT policies too, not just plain SELECT queries. orders has no anon SELECT policy at all (by design — it holds customer PII: name/phone/email/address). submitOrder did `.from("orders").insert({...}).select("order_number").single()` — the INSERT itself now succeeded (after 006/007/008), but the RETURNING was filtered to zero rows by RLS, and `.single()` on zero rows throws a controlled PostgREST error (PGRST116) that submitOrder catches and returns as `{error}` — nothing thrown, so nothing in the browser console, matching the user's report exactly.
bugs.fix: supabase/migrations/010_order_insert_rpc.sql: added create_order(...) as a SECURITY DEFINER function (same pattern as is_admin()/validate_coupon/redeem_coupon) that performs the INSERT and returns only order_number as a scalar — bypasses RLS entirely since it runs as the function owner, and never exposes the orders table itself to anon (no public SELECT policy needed, unlike the naive fix of opening one). submit-order.ts now calls `supabase.rpc("create_order", {...})` instead of `.insert().select().single()`.

bugs.error_message: "permission denied for table coupons" when an admin tried to create a coupon in /admin/coupons
bugs.root_cause: Same bug class as bug-096 (orders) and the earlier gallery_items fix (004) — RLS policy created without the matching table-level GRANT — but this time hitting `authenticated`, disproving the earlier assumption that authenticated already has default privileges in this project (that assumption was only ever confirmed for tables that happened to work, not verified against a GRANT). Hit this exact bug class 3 separate times now, once per table.
bugs.fix: Added supabase/migrations/011_coupons_authenticated_grant.sql: GRANT SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ON coupons TO authenticated, matching the minimal per-table pattern already used for gallery_items (004) and orders (007). (A schema-wide GRANT ALL TABLES + ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES fix was drafted first but reverted — auto-mode correctly flagged it as a broader permission escalation than the user asked for; scoped back to just the coupons table. The systemic pattern — every new table in this project needs an explicit GRANT alongside its RLS policy — stays documented in cerebrum.md as a recurring Do-Not-Repeat check, not as a standing blanket grant.)

bugs.error_message: [submitOrder] result: {error: 'relation "orders" does not exist'} — checkout submission fails after migrations 009/010/011 all applied, coupon creation now works
bugs.root_cause: validate_coupon/redeem_coupon (009) and create_order (010) are SECURITY DEFINER functions that reference `orders`/`coupons` unqualified, relying on the calling session's search_path to resolve them to `public`. SECURITY DEFINER functions run with the owner's privileges but do NOT get a fixed search_path unless one is set explicitly — they inherit whatever search_path is active in the caller's session at execution time. The RPC call itself succeeded (create_order() was found and invoked), but the unqualified `orders` reference inside the function body couldn't be resolved during execution. Direct `.from("orders")` calls elsewhere are unaffected because PostgREST resolves those schema-qualified internally regardless of session search_path.
bugs.fix: supabase/migrations/012_security_definer_search_path.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE all three functions with `SET search_path = public` added and every table reference schema-qualified as `public.orders`/`public.coupons` (belt-and-suspenders, matches Postgres's own documented best practice for SECURITY DEFINER functions). Scoped to only these three — is_admin()/handle_new_user() aren't reported broken. TURNED OUT INCOMPLETE — see bug-107: the same exact error persisted after 012, because a 4th function (generate_order_number(), a trigger fired by the INSERT inside create_order()) was still unqualified and untouched.

bugs.error_message: "relation \"orders\" does not exist" — identical error persists after migration 012, verified via pg_proc that create_order/validate_coupon/redeem_coupon are all correctly public.-qualified with search_path=public in proconfig
bugs.root_cause: generate_order_number() — the BEFORE INSERT trigger function on `orders` from the very first migration (001) — still has an unqualified `FROM orders` and was never touched by migration 012 (which only fixed validate_coupon/redeem_coupon/create_order). It fires as part of the same INSERT INTO public.orders executed inside create_order(), and is the last remaining unqualified reference to `orders` anywhere in the SQL. Diagnosed by asking the user to run `select proname, prosrc, proconfig from pg_proc where proname in (...)` to directly verify the DB state rather than guessing further — confirmed the three RPC functions were correctly fixed, narrowing the remaining suspect to the trigger function.
bugs.fix: supabase/migrations/013_order_number_trigger_search_path.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE generate_order_number() with `FROM public.orders` and `LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public`.

bugs.error_message: Supabase project auto-paused despite weekly keep-alive Vercel Cron being enabled
bugs.root_cause: Two contributing issues, one confirmed and one not fully provable retroactively. (1) UNCONFIRMED: commit a7c1dc2 (2026-07-23) made the CRON_SECRET check fail-closed — if CRON_SECRET was unset in Vercel, the route returned 500 before ever querying Supabase. This was the initial hypothesis, but it was undercut in-session: with the OLD (still fail-closed) code untouched, a manual 'Run' from the Vercel Cron Jobs dashboard returned 200 (CRON_SECRET correct, Supabase reachable) — so we can't prove CRON_SECRET was ever actually missing; Hobby-plan log retention was too short to see historical Monday runs either way. (2) CONFIRMED structural risk, independent of (1): the cron was scheduled weekly (`0 3 * * 1`), exactly matching Supabase's ~7-day pause threshold with zero safety margin. Vercel's own Cron Jobs dashboard states Hobby-plan jobs fire within a 'flexible time window of 1-hour', i.e. exact timing isn't guaranteed — so a single delayed, skipped, or transiently-failed weekly run is sufficient to cross the 7-day threshold and get the project paused even with fully correct code/secrets.
bugs.fix: (a) Rewrote the auth check in app/api/keep-alive/route.ts (and the matching .claude/skills/supabase-keepalive/templates/nextjs-app-router.ts template) to fail OPEN instead of closed: the Supabase ping always executes; a missing/mismatched CRON_SECRET only adds an `authenticated: false` / warning field to the JSON response and a console.warn, it no longer blocks the request. Justified because this route only reads already-public catalog data with the anon key (no mutation, no PII). (b) Changed the cron schedule in vercel.json (and the skill's templates/vercel-json-snippet.json + SKILL.md default) from weekly (`0 3 * * 1`) to daily (`0 3 * * *`) — still within Vercel Hobby's allowed cadence — so a single missed/delayed run can no longer cause a pause; it now takes several consecutive misses. User manually restored the paused Supabase project via its dashboard.
